rationale: The strongest candidates are other letters expressing appreciation for public service, but none supplies distinctive language, a parallel substantive sequence, or reusable administrative machinery material to the child's Senate-wide end-of-session commendation. The similarities are generic conventions of congratulatory or thank-you correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I want to express to the Senate my appreciation for the work they have done.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Please convey to each member of the Joint Committee on the Economic Report my appreciation for the constructive work your committee has done
shared_material.explanation: C18 has the closest wording and also praises congressional work, but this is a routine expression of appreciation and does not extend into a materially shared drafting structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I wish also to thank the members of the Senate
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I want to thank you for a difficult job well done.
shared_material.explanation: C12 shares a conventional thank-you formula for completed public service, without distinctive language or a parallel development.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the results have been well worth while
shared_material.parent_excerpt: And so to you I say: well done. For all that you have achieved you have earned the thanks of your government
shared_material.explanation: C03 similarly commends achievements, but its resignation-acceptance narrative and individualized career review are structurally unlike the child.
